claims.text: Controlled thermal oxidation can form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer on the boride surface.
A continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer will improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
As-fabricated boride components without surface treatment expose the underlying boride directly to molten aluminum.
Pre-oxidation in an oxygen-rich atmosphere at elevated temperature below aluminum's melting point will induce a thin, continuous alumina scale.
Typical operating temperatures for the intended hot-dip aluminum-plating application are approximately 700–750°C.
The protective alumina layer should remain effective at approximately 700–750°C for exposure times encountered in hot-dip aluminum plating.
Minimal mechanical and thermal cycling will help preserve the effectiveness of the alumina layer.
An adherent Al2O3 scale acts as a diffusion barrier to molten-aluminum infiltration into the underlying boride.
The alumina layer reduces direct chemical interaction between molten aluminum and the boride component.
The alumina layer reduces charge-carrier and mass transport across the molten-aluminum/boride interface.
Reduced interfacial transport slows corrosion of the boride component.
Pre-oxidized components will exhibit an approximately 30–50% lower corrosion rate than untreated components under controlled molten-aluminum exposure.
The protective effect depends on controlling oxidation temperature, treatment time, and oxygen partial pressure.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may compromise the integrity of the alumina scale.
Mechanical stress or frequent thermal cycling may compromise the integrity of the alumina scale.
